rationale: DNS hijack and HTTP-redirect injection attacks on SMBs are a documented, recurring threat class with confirmed real-world victims, multiple paid competitors (indicating willingness to pay), and a clear buyer (IT admin or SMB owner) who faces severe reputational and liability consequences. The pain is high-severity even at low frequency because a single undetected incident can redirect customers to phishing pages for hours before discovery. Adjacent SaaS markets (uptime monitoring, DNS monitoring) show SMBs already pay $15–$50/month for comparable proactive alerting.
